title: Maternal Distress during Pregnancy and Offspring Childhood Overweight.
ehr_evidence: We performed a cohort study using prospective data from 37,764 women and child dyads from the Danish National Birth Cohort (1996–2002).
summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between maternal distress during pregnancy and offspring childhood overweight at age 7.
key_findings: No significant association between maternal distress during pregnancy and childhood overweight at age 7 (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96–1.18).
A modest, non-significant increased risk of overweight was observed in boys (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.99–1.33) but not in girls (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.85–1.13).
Maternal worrying during pregnancy was associated with a slightly increased risk of childhood overweight (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00–1.22).
Children of mothers with low or medium socioeconomic status had an increased risk of overweight.
captured_features: maternal anxiety, depression, and stress scores
maternal age, parity, prepregnancy BMI, smoking, exercise, gestational weight gain, breastfeeding duration
population: 37,764 mother-child dyads from the Danish National Birth Cohort, children aged approximately 7 years
limitations: potential selection bias due to 40% loss to follow-up
relatively low exposure contrast in a healthy, high-SES cohort
single time-point measurement of childhood overweight
